subject: Whether reading the track header deeper would find a track-type signal
question: Does a type signal appear below the depth-4 radius the classifier searches?

reverify.command: For each AXLayoutItem whose AXHelp begins with the track-header string, collect AXDescription/AXTitle/AXHelp/AXIdentifier/AXRoleDescription/AXValue over its whole subtree to depth 8, then diff the token sets between a known audio track and a known software instrument.
reverify.expected: the sets differ only in the track name, and in track-stack tokens where one of them is a stack
reverify.cost: ~4 min with a project carrying both track kinds; read-only

method: The earlier reading stopped at depth 4 because that is what the classifier searches, which left 'a signal exists deeper' open as a design option. Went deeper before choosing, so the choice rests on a measurement rather than on the absence of one.

tracks: Absolute Zero (software instrument, a track stack)

observations.what: tokens unique to the audio track
observations.note: the track name and its ordinal, nothing else

observations.what: tokens unique to one software instrument
observations.note: the track name and its ordinal

observations.what: tokens unique to the other software instrument
observations.note: a track stack's disclosure arrow, not anything about being an instrument

observations.what: what the classifier does with this

conclusion: Reading deeper does not help. At depth 8 the three headers share 135 tokens, and every token unique to one of them is either the track's own name or, for the one track that is a stack, the stack disclosure arrow. Nothing distinguishes an audio track from a software instrument at any depth the header offers, so widening the classifier's radius was not a design option and is now ruled out by measurement rather than by not having looked. What remains is to stop answering: the aggregate satisfies 2 label sets on every header, and where more than one matches the honest answer is unknown.
limits: Three headers in one project, ko-KR. Two of the three are software instruments and only one is an audio track, so 'the audio track has no distinguishing token' rests on a single example.
One of the instrument tracks is a track stack, which is why its unique-token count is larger; a non-stack comparison would be cleaner and was not available in this project.
Depth 8 was chosen as comfortably past the classifier's 4. It is not a proof that no depth whatsoever carries a signal, only that the ones a reader would plausibly widen to do not.
This says nothing about where the type IS readable. The channel strip carries a partial signal, measured separately, and reading it needs the Mixer revealed.
